'''Pierre Colmez''' (born 1962) is a French [[mathematician]] and ''[[directeur de recherche]]'' at the [[CNRS]] ([[Institut de mathématiques de Jussieu – Paris Rive Gauche|IMJ-PRG]]) known for his work in [[number theory]] and [[p-adic analysis|''p''-adic analysis]].

==Education==
Colmez studied at [[École Normale Supérieure]] and obtained his [[doctorate]] from the [[Grenoble Alpes University|University of Grenoble]].

==Research==
He works on special values of L-functions and <math>p</math>-adic representations of <math>p</math>-adic groups at the meeting point of Fontaine's and Langlands' programs. His contributions include:

* A proof of a <math>p</math>-adic analog of Dirichlet's analytic [[class number formula]].<ref>Résidu en s=1 des fonctions zêta p-adiques, Inventiones mathematicae 91 (1988), 371-389</ref>
* A conjecture: the '''Colmez conjecture''' relating Artin L-functions at <math>s=0</math> and periods of abelian varieties with complex multiplication, a far-reaching generalization of the [[Chowla-Selberg formula]].<ref>Périodes des variétés abéliennes à multiplication complexe, Annals of Mathematics 138 (1993), 625–683</ref>
* A proof of [[Bernadette Perrin-Riou|Perrin-Riou's]] conjectural explicit reciprocity law related to the functional equation of <math>p</math>-adic L-functions.<ref>Théorie d'Iwasawa des représentations de de Rham d'un corps local, Annals of Mathematics 148 (1998), 485–571</ref>
* Several contributions to [[Jean-Marc Fontaine|Fontaine's]] program of classification of <math>p</math>-adic representations of the [[absolute Galois group]] of a finite extension of <math>\mathbb{Q}_p</math>, including proofs of conjectures of Fontaine such as "weakly admissible implies admissible"<ref>Construction des représentations p-adiques semi-stables (avec J.-M. Fontaine), Inventiones mathematicae 140 (2000), 1–43 (avec [[Jean-Marc Fontaine]])</ref> and the "<math>p</math>-adic monodromy conjecture" which describe representations coming from geometry, or the overconvergence of all representations,<ref>Espaces Vectoriels de dimension finie et représentations de de Rham, Astérisque 319 (2008), 117–186</ref><ref>Représentations p-adiques surconvergentes, Inventiones mathematicae 133 (1998), 581–611 (avec Frédéric Cherbonnier)</ref> and the addition of new concepts such as "trianguline representations"<ref>Représentations triangulines de dimension 2, Astérisque 319 (2008), 213–258</ref> or "Banach-Colmez spaces".<ref>Espaces de Banach de dimension finie, Journal Institut de Mathématiques de Jussieu 1 (2002), 331–439</ref><ref>Arthur-César Le Bras, Espaces de Banach–Colmez et faisceaux cohérents sur la courbe de Fargues–Fontaine, Duke Math. J. 167 (2018), 3455-3532</ref>
* A construction of the <math>p</math>-adic local [[Langlands program|Langlands correspondence]] for <math>\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)</math>, via the construction of a functor (known as "Colmez's functor" or "Colmez's Montreal functor"<ref>Vytautas Paškūnas, The image of Colmez’s Montreal functor, Publications mathématiques de l'IHÉS 118 (2013), 1–191</ref>) from representation of <math>\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)</math> to representations of the absolute Galois group of <math>\mathbb{Q}_p</math>.<ref>Représentations de <math>\mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}_p)</math> et <math>(\varphi,\Gamma)</math>-modules, Astérisque 330 (2010), 281–509</ref>
* Comparison theorems for <math>p</math>-adic algebraic and analytic varieties with applications to a geometrization of the <math>p</math>-adic local Langlands correspondence.<ref><math>p</math>-adic vanishing cycles and syntomic cohomology, Inventiones mathematicae 208 (2017), 1-108 (with [[Wiesława Nizioł]]).</ref><ref>Cohomologie <math>p</math>-adique de la tour de Drinfeld, le cas de la dimension 1, Journal of the AMS 33 (2020), 311–362 (with [[Wiesława Nizioł]] and Gabriel Dospinescu).</ref><ref>Cohomology of <math>p</math>-adic Stein spaces, Inventiones mathematicae 219 (2020), 873–985 (with [[Wiesława Nizioł]] and Gabriel Dospinescu).</ref>

With [[Jean-Pierre Serre]], he co-edited the ''Correspondance Grothendieck-Serre '' (2001)<ref>{{cite journal|author=Raynaud, Michel|authorlink=Michel Raynaud|title=Book Review: ''Correspondance Grothendieck-Serre ''|journal=Notices of the AMS|date=October 2003|volume=50|issue=9|pages=1085–1086|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200309/rev-raynaud.pdf}}</ref><ref name="GrothendieckColmez2004">{{cite book|editor2=Serre, J.-P.|editor1=Colmez, P.|title=Grothendieck-Serre Correspondence|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=EiB6Q5P4RRkC|year=2004|publisher=American Mathematical Society; Société Mathématique de France|isbn=978-0-8218-3424-4|postscript=; bilingual edition}}</ref> and the ''Correspondance Serre-Tate ''(2015).<ref>Documents Mathématiques 13, 14, Société Mathématique de France, 2015</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Colmez won the 2005 [[Fermat Prize]] for his contributions to the study of [[L-functions]] and p-adic [[Galois representations]].

In 1998, he was an [[invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Berlin.<ref>{{cite book|author=Colmez, Pierre|chapter=Représentations ''p''-adiques d'un corps local|title=Doc. Math. (Bielefeld) Extra Vol. ICM Berlin, 1998, vol. II|year=1998|pages=153–162|chapter-url=https://www.elibm.org/ft/10011650000}}</ref>

Colmez has won the French [[Go (game)|Go]] championship four times.<ref>[http://ffg.jeudego.org/informations/competitions/chp_histo.php Open - Fédération Française de Go - Jeu de go]</ref>

==Personal life==
Pierre Colmez and [[Leila Schneps]] are the parents of [[Coralie Colmez]].<ref>{{cite news |url= https://www.economist.com/prospero/2013/05/02/allow-me-to-explain-your-honour |publisher=[[The Economist]] |title= Allow me to explain, Your Honour |date=2 May 2013 |accessdate=2 October 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.thecut.com/2018/01/interview-with-unifrog-founder-coralie-colmez.html |title= The Mathematician Who Moonlights As a Rock-Band Violinist |first=Diana |last=Tsui |publisher=[[The Cut (website)|The Cut]] |date=9 January 2018 |accessdate=2 October 2020}}</ref> Violinist [[David Grimal]] is Colmez's first cousin.
